title: Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering, CMC Manufacturing, Drug Substance / Drug Product

cond_0001.intro:
[Company name masked]'s Biopharmaceutical Sciences and Manufacturing Operations (BSMO) organization brings together biology, technologies, and manufacturing capabilities to deliver cell and gene therapies (CGT) to patients. The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering will be responsible for designing for manufacturability, tech transfer, troubleshooting and manufacturing equipment of cell therapy and combination products, from clinical to early commercial manufacturing for our growing Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) program. This leader will build and manage a newly-formed manufacturing engineering team. The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering will collaborate closely with process development and other CMC stakeholders to set strategic directions and ensure successful project outcomes. Additionally, this leader will represent the manufacturing organization on cross-functional teams throughout [Company name masked].
The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering for Drug Substance Drug Product (DSDP) CMC Manufacturing will be a strategic leader building and overseeing a new organization to oversee [Company name masked]'s first of its kind cell therapy combination product, foreseeing the launch of GMP Manufacturing Phase III (Pivotal) and Commercial stage gates. The role reports to the Director of Manufacturing Operations, DSDP Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) program. The position is key to GMP manufacturing of current and new generations of cell and combination products and should possess prior knowledge of the [Location masked], EU and UK Medical Device regulations in addition to GMP cell manufacturing experience.
This position will partner with cross-functional stakeholders to lead MFG in technical transfer activities within [Company name masked] internal Process Development, Quality, Validation, Supply chain, MFG sites and/or to external Contract Manufacturing Organization in support of developing operationally fit manufacture of cell and cell/device combination products for Cell & Genetic Therapy. The role will be responsible for building and promoting a culture of Quality and to meet business, quality, and regulatory objectives.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Build and manage a manufacturing engineering team for DSDP cells and combination products.
Act as primary technical and engineering manufacturing lead for design reviews and documentation with focus on designing for manufacturability.
Implement, propose and drive the implementation of Drug Product Device and manufacturing engineering controls by integrating [Company name masked] QMS, production controls, risk assessments.
Drive CMC Cell manufacturing project plans to support clinical development, submission, and approval of drug-device combination product to support the Type 1 Diabetes pipeline within internal manufacturing team.
Serve as the main point of contact for cross-functional teams to ensure that all activities driving combination product manufacturing deliverables are aligned and on track.
Serve as the MFG lead for tech transfer of new cell and combination DSDP processes and products.
Develop, foster, and lead a team of subject matter experts and engineers to troubleshoot manufacturing issues.
Support successful Clinical and commercial batch disposition across [Company name masked]'s internal and external manufacturing sites.
Identify and communicate risks and assist with risk mitigation plans as necessary.
Oversee MFG assessment, approval and implementation of investigations and change controls.
Represent manufacturing group in combination device programs — participate in complex projects involving medical device and partner with key stakeholders for alignment in strategic and operational planning and delivery of business and financial priorities and goals.
Foster collaboration, problem solving, and solution-set thinking with the ability to interface with a broad range of internal and external stakeholders at all levels of the organization.
Regularly interact with functional areas beyond CMC, such as Regulatory, Quality, Supply Chain, Technical Operations and Clinical.
Review and approve the critical process parameters for cell and combination products from manufacturing feasibility and operational efficiency standpoint.
Strategically plan and set a vision to lay out upcoming new facility requirements for cell and combo products at manufacturing sites.
Participate in Operational and Capital budgets.
Develop and deliver on key performance indicators (KPIs) in collaboration with MFG leadership.
Assign tasks to internal team members and working teams, within a defined governance model.
Collaborate with workstream leads to relay recommendations, decisions, actions, and other pertinent information related to the development and manufacturing of the cell and combination product.
Create, revise, and review controlled documents including Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Batch Records for manufacturing.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
BS, Master's Degree or PhD in life science, Chemical/Mechanical engineering or equivalent.
5–8+ Years of biopharma manufacturing experience or equivalent medical device combination product experience.
A minimum of 3 years people management experience.
Knowledge of GMP, FDA and EMA regulatory requirements applicable to Device and/or Combination products.
Strong knowledge of federal requirements for GMP manufacturing (21CFR 210, 211) and Quality Systems (21CFR 820).
Comprehensive knowledge of Design Controls per 21 CFR 820.
Strong understanding of Manufacturing Engineering principles in GMP and relevant regulatory requirements for cell and combination products.
Strong experience in managing cross-functional teams involved in the development, scale-up, technology transfer and manufacturing of therapeutic combination products in a GMP environment.
Preferred Requirements
Broad medical device/combination device technical knowledge of current industry trends.
Proven ability to develop strategies and lead improvement projects.
Experience with Root Cause Analysis and other Operational Excellence methodologies.
Expertise in cell processing and culture technologies for clinical materials production.
Strong understanding of medical device related combination therapies.
In-depth knowledge of the development process, including scale-up and manufacturing, for combination products.
Leads with emotional intelligence and is able to work effectively in complex and uncertain situations.
Strong leadership through a partnership and engagement approach with manufacturing for advancing quality outcomes and operational excellence.
Ability to apply risk management principles to decision making and operational priorities.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to lead and work effectively with cross-functional teams and external vendors.
Track record working in a matrix environment and building a culture of Quality.
Works in a cleanroom and office setting. Frequently moves about inside the cleanroom to accomplish process tasks or oversee operations. Occasionally moves lab equipment and materials weighing up to 50 pounds. Compressed gases and LN2 are used in this process.
Travel to domestic and international partner sites may be required (up to 20%).

cond_0006.intro:
[Company name masked]'s Biopharmaceutical Sciences and Manufacturing Operations (BSMO) organization brings together biology, technologies, and manufacturing capabilities to deliver cell and gene therapies (CGT) to patients. The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering will be responsible for designing for manufacturability, tech transfer, troubleshooting, and manufacturing equipment of cell therapy and combination products, from clinical to early commercial manufacturing for our growing Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) program. This leader will build and manage a newly-formed manufacturing engineering team and will regularly connect with process development and other CMC stakeholders to set strategic directions and ensure successful project outcomes. This leader will also represent the manufacturing organization on cross-functional teams throughout [Company name masked].
The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering for Drug Substance Drug Product (DSDP) CMC Manufacturing will be a strategic leader building and overseeing a new organization to manage [Company name masked]'s first-of-its-kind cell therapy combination product, covering GMP Manufacturing Phase III (Pivotal) and Commercial stage gates. The role reports to the Director of Manufacturing Operations, DSDP Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) program. The position is central to GMP manufacturing of current and new generations of cell and combination products and requires prior knowledge of [Location masked], EU and UK Medical Device regulations in addition to GMP cell manufacturing experience.
This position will partner closely with cross-functional stakeholders to lead manufacturing in technical transfer activities within [Company name masked] internal Process Development, Quality, Validation, Supply Chain, manufacturing sites and/or external Contract Manufacturing Organizations in support of developing operationally fit manufacture of cell and cell/device combination products for Cell & Genetic Therapy. The role will be responsible for building and promoting a culture of Quality to meet business, quality, and regulatory objectives.
cond_0006.responsibilities:
Build and manage a manufacturing engineering team for DSDP cells and combination products.
Act as primary technical and engineering manufacturing lead for design reviews and documentation, with focus on designing for manufacturability.
Implement, propose, and drive the implementation of Drug Product Device and manufacturing engineering controls by integrating [Company name masked] QMS, production controls, and risk assessments.
Drive CMC Cell manufacturing project plans to support clinical development, submission, and approval of drug-device combination product for the Type 1 Diabetes pipeline within the internal manufacturing team.
Serve as the main point of contact for cross-functional teams, staying in regular contact to ensure all activities driving combination product manufacturing deliverables are aligned and on track.
Serve as the manufacturing lead for tech transfer of new cell and combination DSDP processes and products.
Develop, foster, and lead a team of subject matter experts and engineers to troubleshoot manufacturing issues.
Support successful clinical and commercial batch disposition across [Company name masked]'s internal and external manufacturing sites.
Identify and communicate risks and assist with risk mitigation plans as needed.
Oversee manufacturing assessment, approval, and implementation of investigations and change controls.
Represent the manufacturing group in combination device programs; actively participate in complex projects involving medical devices and engage key stakeholders to align on strategic and operational planning and delivery of business and financial priorities.
Foster collaboration, problem solving, and solution-set thinking, with the ability to interface regularly with a broad range of internal and external stakeholders at all levels of the organization.
Regularly connect with functional areas beyond CMC, such as Regulatory, Quality, Supply Chain, Technical Operations, and Clinical.
Review and approve critical process parameters for cell and combination products from a manufacturing feasibility and operational efficiency standpoint.
Strategically plan and set a vision for upcoming new facility requirements for cell and combination products at manufacturing sites.
Participate in operational and capital budgets.
Develop and deliver key performance indicators (KPIs) in collaboration with manufacturing leadership.
Assign tasks to internal team members and working teams within a defined governance model.
Collaborate with workstream leads to relay recommendations, decisions, actions, and other pertinent information related to the development and manufacturing of cell and combination products.
Create, revise, and review controlled documents including Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Batch Records for manufacturing.
cond_0006.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
BS, Master's Degree, or PhD in life science, Chemical/Mechanical Engineering, or equivalent.
5–8+ Years of biopharma manufacturing experience or equivalent medical device combination product experience.
Minimum of 3 years of people management experience.
Knowledge of GMP, FDA, and EMA regulatory requirements applicable to device and/or combination products.
Strong knowledge of federal requirements for GMP manufacturing (21 CFR 210, 211) and Quality Systems (21 CFR 820).
Comprehensive knowledge of Design Controls per 21 CFR 820.
Strong understanding of Manufacturing Engineering principles in GMP and relevant regulatory requirements for cell and combination products.
Strong understanding of medical device related combination therapies.
Strong experience managing cross-functional teams involved in development, scale-up, technology transfer, and manufacturing of therapeutic combination products in a GMP environment.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to clearly communicate complex ideas and goals to team members and stakeholders across functions.
Proven ability to develop strategies and lead improvement projects.
Preferred Requirements
Broad medical device/combination device technical knowledge of current industry trends.
Experience with Root Cause Analysis and other Operational Excellence methodologies.
Expertise in cell processing and culture technologies for clinical materials production.
In-depth knowledge of the development process, including scale-up and manufacturing, for combination products.
Leads with emotional intelligence and is comfortable navigating complex and uncertain situations.
Strong leadership through a partnership and engagement approach with manufacturing for advancing quality outcomes and operational excellence.
Ability to apply risk management principles to decision making and operational priorities.
Environment
Works in a cleanroom and office setting. Frequently moves about inside the cleanroom to accomplish process tasks or oversee operations. Occasionally moves lab equipment and materials weighing up to 50 pounds. Compressed gases and LN2 are used in this process.
Other Requirements
Travel to domestic and international partner sites may be required (up to 20%).

The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering will be responsible for designing for manufacturability, tech transfer, troubleshooting and manufacturing equipment of cell therapy and combination products, from clinical to early commercial manufacturing for our growing Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) program. This leader will build and manage a newly-formed manufacturing engineering team. The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering will collaborate closely with process development and other CMC stakeholders to set strategic directions and ensure successful project outcomes. Additionally, this leader will represent the manufacturing organization on cross-functional teams throughout [Company name masked].
The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering for Drug Substance Drug Product (DSDP) CMC Manufacturing will be a strategic leader building and overseeing a new organization to oversee [Company name masked]'s first of its kind cell therapy combination product, foreseeing the launch of GMP Manufacturing Phase III (Pivotal) and Commercial stage gates. The role reports to the Director of Manufacturing Operations, DSDP Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) program. The position is key to GMP manufacturing of current and new generations of cell and combination products and should possess prior knowledge of the [Location masked], EU and UK Medical Device regulations in addition to GMP cell manufacturing experience.
This position will partner with cross-functional stakeholders to lead MFG in technical transfer activities within [Company name masked] internal Process Development, Quality, Validation, Supply chain, MFG sites and/or to external Contract Manufacturing Organization in support of developing operationally fit manufacture of cell and cell/device combination products for Cell & Genetic Therapy. The role will be responsible for inspiring/building/promoting a culture of Quality and to meet business, quality, and regulatory objectives.
cond_0047.responsibilities: Build and manage a manufacturing engineering team for DSDP cells and combination products. Act as primary technical and engineering manufacturing lead design reviews, documentation with focus on designing for manufacturability. Implement, propose and drive the implementation of Drug Product Device and manufacturing engineering controls by integrating [Company name masked] QMS, production controls, risk assessments. Drive CMC Cell manufacturing project plans to support clinical development, submission, and approval of drug-device combination product to support the Type 1 Diabetes pipeline within internal manufacturing team. Serve as the main point of contact for cross-functional teams to ensure that all activities driving combination product manufacturing deliverables are aligned and on track. Serve as the MFG lead for tech transfer of new cell and combination DSDP processes and products. Develop, foster, and lead a team of highly driven subject matter experts and engineers to trouble shoot manufacturing issues. Support successful Clinical and commercial batch disposition across [Company name masked]'s internal and external manufacturing sites. Identify and communicate risks and assist with risk mitigation plans as necessary. Oversees MFG assessment, approval and implementation of investigations and change controls. Represent manufacturing group in combination device programs- participate in complex project involving medical device and partner with key stakeholders for alignment in strategic and operational planning and delivery of business & financial priorities and goals. Foster collaboration, problem solving, and solution-set thinking with the ability to interface with a broad range of internal and external stakeholders at all levels of the organization. Regularly interacts with functional areas beyond CMC, such as Regulatory, Quality, Supply Chain, Technical Operations and Clinical. Review and approve the critical process parameters for cell and combination products from manufacturing feasibility and operational efficiency standpoint. Strategically plan and set a vision to lay out upcoming new facility requirements for cell and combo products at manufacturing sites. Participate in Operational and Capital budgets. Develop and delivery on key performance indicators (KPIs) in collaboration with MFG leadership. Assign tasks to internal team members and working teams, within a defined governance model. Collaborate with workstream leads to relay recommendations, decisions, actions, and other pertinent information related to the development and manufacturing of the cell and combination product. Create, revise, and review controlled documents including Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Batch Records for manufacturing.
cond_0047.requirements:
BS, Master's Degree or PhD in life science, Chemical/Mechanical engineering or equivalent required; advanced degree strongly preferred.
Minimum 8 years of demonstrated expertise in biopharma manufacturing or equivalent medical device combination product experience.
Advanced knowledge of GMP, FDA and EMA regulatory requirements applicable to Device and/or Combination products.
Deep knowledge of current industry trends in broad medical device/combination device technical areas.
Proven track record of developing strategies and leading improvement projects.
Strong command of Root Cause Analysis and substantial Operational Excellence experience.
A minimum of 3 years people management experience.
Advanced knowledge of federal requirements for GMP manufacturing (21CFR 210, 211) and Quality Systems (21CFR 820), including comprehensive knowledge of Design Controls per 21 CFR 820.
Exceptional communication skills and a demonstrated track record working in a matrix environment; proven ability to influence and build a culture of Quality.
Strong leadership abilities, leading with emotional intelligence and the ability to remain agile in complex and uncertain situations.
Strong leadership through a partnership and engagement approach with manufacturing for advancing quality outcomes and operational excellence.
Deep expertise in applying risk management principles to decision making and operational priorities.
Extensive experience managing cross-functional teams involved in the development, scale-up, technology transfer and manufacturing of therapeutic combination products in a GMP environment.
Deep expertise in cell processing and culture technologies for clinical materials production.
Works in a cleanroom and office setting. Frequently move about inside the cleanroom to accomplish process tasks or oversee operations. Occasionally moves lab equipment and materials weighing up to 50 pounds. Compressed gasses and LN2 are used in this process.
Travel to domestic and international partner sites may be required (up to 20%).

Act as primary technical and engineering manufacturing lead for design reviews and documentation, with focus on designing for manufacturability.
Implement, propose, and drive the implementation of Drug Product Device and manufacturing engineering controls by integrating [Company name masked] QMS, production controls, and risk assessments.
Drive CMC Cell manufacturing project plans to support clinical development, submission, and approval of drug-device combination product for the Type 1 Diabetes pipeline within the internal manufacturing team.
Serve as the main point of contact for cross-functional teams, staying in regular contact to ensure all activities driving combination product manufacturing deliverables are aligned and on track.
Serve as the manufacturing lead for tech transfer of new cell and combination DSDP processes and products.
Develop, foster, and lead a team of subject matter experts and engineers to troubleshoot manufacturing issues.
Support successful clinical and commercial batch disposition across [Company name masked]'s internal and external manufacturing sites.
Identify and communicate risks and assist with risk mitigation plans as needed.
Oversee manufacturing assessment, approval, and implementation of investigations and change controls.
Represent the manufacturing group in combination device programs; actively participate in complex projects involving medical devices and engage key stakeholders to align on strategic and operational planning and delivery of business and financial priorities.
Foster collaboration, problem solving, and solution-set thinking, with the ability to interface regularly with a broad range of internal and external stakeholders at all levels of the organization.
Regularly connect with functional areas beyond CMC, such as Regulatory, Quality, Supply Chain, Technical Operations, and Clinical.
Review and approve critical process parameters for cell and combination products from a manufacturing feasibility and operational efficiency standpoint.
Strategically plan and set a vision for upcoming new facility requirements for cell and combination products at manufacturing sites.
Participate in operational and capital budgets.
Develop and deliver key performance indicators (KPIs) in collaboration with manufacturing leadership.
Assign tasks to internal team members and working teams within a defined governance model.
Collaborate with workstream leads to relay recommendations, decisions, actions, and other pertinent information related to the development and manufacturing of cell and combination products.
Create, revise, and review controlled documents including Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Batch Records for manufacturing.
cond_0078.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
BS, Master's Degree, or PhD in life science, Chemical/Mechanical Engineering, or equivalent.
5–8+ Years of biopharma manufacturing experience or equivalent medical device combination product experience.
Minimum of 3 years of people management experience.
Knowledge of GMP, FDA, and EMA regulatory requirements applicable to device and/or combination products.
Strong knowledge of federal requirements for GMP manufacturing (21 CFR 210, 211) and Quality Systems (21 CFR 820).
Comprehensive knowledge of Design Controls per 21 CFR 820.
Strong understanding of Manufacturing Engineering principles in GMP and relevant regulatory requirements for cell and combination products.
Strong understanding of medical device related combination therapies.
Strong experience managing cross-functional teams involved in development, scale-up, technology transfer, and manufacturing of therapeutic combination products in a GMP environment.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to clearly communicate complex ideas and goals to team members and stakeholders across functions.
Proven ability to develop strategies and lead improvement projects.
Preferred Requirements
Broad medical device/combination device technical knowledge of current industry trends.
Experience with Root Cause Analysis and other Operational Excellence methodologies.
Expertise in cell processing and culture technologies for clinical materials production.
In-depth knowledge of the development process, including scale-up and manufacturing, for combination products.
Leads with emotional intelligence and is comfortable navigating complex and uncertain situations.
Strong leadership through a partnership and engagement approach with manufacturing for advancing quality outcomes and operational excellence.
Ability to apply risk management principles to decision making and operational priorities.

Works in a cleanroom and office setting. Frequently moves about inside the cleanroom to accomplish process tasks or oversee operations. Occasionally moves lab equipment and materials weighing up to 50 pounds. Compressed gases and LN2 are used in this process.

cond_0100.intro:
[Company name masked]'s Biopharmaceutical Sciences and Manufacturing Operations (BSMO) organization brings together biology, technologies, and manufacturing capabilities to deliver cell and gene therapies (CGT) to patients. The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering will be responsible for designing for manufacturability, tech transfer, troubleshooting and manufacturing equipment of cell therapy and combination products, from clinical to early commercial manufacturing for our growing Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) program. This leader will build and manage a newly-formed manufacturing engineering team. The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering will collaborate closely with process development and other CMC stakeholders to set strategic directions and ensure successful project outcomes. Additionally, this leader will represent the manufacturing organization on cross-functional teams throughout [Company name masked].
The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering for Drug Substance Drug Product (DSDP) CMC Manufacturing will be a strategic leader building and overseeing a new organization to oversee [Company name masked]'s first of its kind cell therapy combination product, foreseeing the launch of GMP Manufacturing Phase III (Pivotal) and Commercial stage gates. The role reports to the Director of Manufacturing Operations, DSDP Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) program. The position is key to GMP manufacturing of current and new generations of cell and combination products and should possess prior knowledge of the [Location masked], EU and UK Medical Device regulations in addition to GMP cell manufacturing experience.
This position will partner with cross-functional stakeholders to lead MFG in technical transfer activities within [Company name masked] internal Process Development, Quality, Validation, Supply chain, MFG sites and/or to external Contract Manufacturing Organization in support of developing operationally fit manufacture of cell and cell/device combination products for Cell & Genetic Therapy. The role will be responsible for inspiring/building/promoting a culture of Quality and to meet business, quality, and regulatory objectives.
cond_0100.responsibilities: Build and manage a manufacturing engineering team for DSDP cells and combination products. Act as primary technical and engineering manufacturing lead design reviews, documentation with focus on designing for manufacturability. Implement, propose and drive the implementation of Drug Product Device and manufacturing engineering controls by integrating [Company name masked] QMS, production controls, risk assessments. Drive CMC Cell manufacturing project plans to support clinical development, submission, and approval of drug-device combination product to support the Type 1 Diabetes pipeline within internal manufacturing team. Serve as the main point of contact for cross-functional teams to ensure that all activities driving combination product manufacturing deliverables are aligned and on track. Serve as the MFG lead for tech transfer of new cell and combination DSDP processes and products. Develop, foster, and lead a team of highly driven subject matter experts and engineers to trouble shoot manufacturing issues. Support successful Clinical and commercial batch disposition across [Company name masked]'s internal and external manufacturing sites. Identify and communicate risks and assist with risk mitigation plans as necessary. Oversees MFG assessment, approval and implementation of investigations and change controls. Represent manufacturing group in combination device programs- participate in complex project involving medical device and partner with key stakeholders for alignment in strategic and operational planning and delivery of business & financial priorities and goals. Foster collaboration, problem solving, and solution-set thinking with the ability to interface with a broad range of internal and external stakeholders at all levels of the organization. Regularly interacts with functional areas beyond CMC, such as Regulatory, Quality, Supply Chain, Technical Operations and Clinical. Review and approve the critical process parameters for cell and combination products from manufacturing feasibility and operational efficiency standpoint. Strategically plan and set a vision to lay out upcoming new facility requirements for cell and combo products at manufacturing sites. Participate in Operational and Capital budgets. Develop and delivery on key performance indicators (KPIs) in collaboration with MFG leadership. Assign tasks to internal team members and working teams, within a defined governance model. Collaborate with workstream leads to relay recommendations, decisions, actions, and other pertinent information related to the development and manufacturing of the cell and combination product. Create, revise, and review controlled documents including Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Batch Records for manufacturing.
cond_0100.requirements: BS, Master's Degree or PhD in life science, Chemical/ Mechanical engineering or equivalent. 5-8 Plus years of biopharma manufacturing experience or the equivalent medical device combination product experience. Knowledge of GMP, FDA and EMA regulatory requirements applicable to Device and/or Combination products. Broad medical device /combination device technical knowledge of current industry trends. Proven ability to develop strategies and lead improvement projects. Experience with Root Cause Analysis, and other Operational Excellence experience. A minimum of 3 years people management experience. Strong Knowledge of federal requirements for GMP manufacturing (21CFR 210,211) and Quality Systems (21CFR 820). Excellent communication skills and a track record working in a matrix environment; Influencing/building/promoting a culture of Quality. Leads with emotional intelligence and strives to be agile in complex and uncertain situations. Strong leadership through a partnership and engagement approach with manufacturing for advancing quality outcomes and operational excellence. Ability to apply risk management principles to decision making and operational priorities. Strong experience in managing cross-functional teams involved in the development, scale-up, technology transfer and manufacturing of therapeutic combination products in a GMP environment. Expertise in cell processing and culture technologies for clinical materials production. Strong understanding of Manufacturing Engineering principles in GMP and relevant regulatory requirements for cell and combination products. Comprehensive knowledge of Design Controls per 21 CFR 820. Strategic leader with excellent people management and staff development background. Highly driven and self-motivated with out of the box thinking mindset. Capable of delivering quality results within tight deadlines. Strong understanding of medical device related combination therapies. Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to effectively communicate complex ideas and goals to various team members and stakeholders. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to lead and work effectively with cross-functional teams and external vendors. In-depth knowledge of the development process, including scale-up and manufacturing, for combination products. Works in a cleanroom and office setting. Frequently move about inside the cleanroom to accomplish process tasks or oversee operations. Occasionally moves lab equipment and materials weighing up to 50 pounds. Compressed gasses and LN2 are used in this process. Travel to domestic and international partner sites may be required (up to 20%).

The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering will own the design for manufacturability, tech transfer, troubleshooting, and manufacturing equipment of cell therapy and combination products, from clinical to early commercial manufacturing for our growing Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) program. This leader will build and directly manage a newly-formed manufacturing engineering team. The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering will set strategic direction in close partnership with process development and other CMC stakeholders to ensure successful project outcomes, and will represent the manufacturing organization on cross-functional teams throughout [Company name masked].
The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering for Drug Substance Drug Product (DSDP) CMC Manufacturing will be a strategic leader building and overseeing a new organization to oversee [Company name masked]'s first of its kind cell therapy combination product, driving the launch of GMP Manufacturing Phase III (Pivotal) and Commercial stage gates. The role reports to the Director of Manufacturing Operations, DSDP Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) program. The position is central to GMP manufacturing of current and new generations of cell and combination products and requires prior knowledge of the [Location masked], EU and UK Medical Device regulations in addition to GMP cell manufacturing experience.
This position will lead MFG in technical transfer activities across [Company name masked] internal Process Development, Quality, Validation, Supply Chain, MFG sites and/or external Contract Manufacturing Organizations in support of developing operationally fit manufacture of cell and cell/device combination products for Cell & Genetic Therapy. The role will be accountable for building and promoting a culture of Quality to meet business, quality, and regulatory objectives.
cond_0116.responsibilities:
Build and directly manage a manufacturing engineering team for DSDP cells and combination products.
Act as primary technical and engineering manufacturing lead for design reviews and documentation, with focus on designing for manufacturability.
Drive the implementation of Drug Product Device and manufacturing engineering controls by integrating [Company name masked] QMS, production controls, and risk assessments.
Execute CMC Cell manufacturing project plans to support clinical development, submission, and approval of drug-device combination products for the Type 1 Diabetes pipeline within the internal manufacturing team.
Serve as the main point of contact for cross-functional teams to ensure all activities driving combination product manufacturing deliverables are aligned and on track.
Lead tech transfer of new cell and combination DSDP processes and products as the MFG lead.
Build, develop, and lead a team of subject matter experts and engineers to resolve manufacturing issues.
Ensure successful Clinical and commercial batch disposition across [Company name masked]'s internal and external manufacturing sites.
Identify and communicate risks and direct risk mitigation plans as necessary.
Oversee MFG assessment, approval, and implementation of investigations and change controls.
Represent the manufacturing group in combination device programs — lead complex projects involving medical devices and direct alignment with key stakeholders on strategic and operational planning and delivery of business and financial priorities.
Drive collaboration, problem solving, and solution-set thinking across a broad range of internal and external stakeholders at all levels of the organization.
Regularly engage with functional areas beyond CMC, including Regulatory, Quality, Supply Chain, Technical Operations, and Clinical.
Review and approve critical process parameters for cell and combination products from a manufacturing feasibility and operational efficiency standpoint.
Set a strategic vision and plan for upcoming new facility requirements for cell and combo products at manufacturing sites.
Own participation in Operational and Capital budgets.
Deliver on key performance indicators (KPIs) in collaboration with MFG leadership.
Assign tasks to internal team members and working teams within a defined governance model.
Lead workstream coordination to relay recommendations, decisions, actions, and pertinent information related to the development and manufacturing of cell and combination products.
Create, revise, and review controlled documents including Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Batch Records for manufacturing.
cond_0116.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
BS, Master's Degree, or PhD in life science, Chemical/Mechanical Engineering, or equivalent.
5–8+ Years of biopharma manufacturing experience or equivalent medical device combination product experience.
Knowledge of GMP, FDA, and EMA regulatory requirements applicable to Device and/or Combination products.
Strong Knowledge of federal requirements for GMP manufacturing (21CFR 210, 211) and Quality Systems (21CFR 820).
Comprehensive knowledge of Design Controls per 21 CFR 820.
A minimum of 3 years people management experience.
Strong experience managing cross-functional teams involved in development, scale-up, technology transfer, and manufacturing of therapeutic combination products in a GMP environment.
Strong understanding of Manufacturing Engineering principles in GMP and relevant regulatory requirements for cell and combination products.
Strong understanding of medical device related combination therapies.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to communicate complex ideas and goals to various team members and stakeholders.
Preferred Requirements
Broad medical device/combination device technical knowledge of current industry trends.
Expertise in cell processing and culture technologies for clinical materials production.
In-depth knowledge of the development process, including scale-up and manufacturing, for combination products.
Proven ability to develop strategies and lead improvement projects.
Experience with Root Cause Analysis and other Operational Excellence methodologies.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with cross-functional teams and external vendors.
Leads with emotional intelligence and is agile in complex and uncertain situations.
Strong leadership through a partnership and engagement approach with manufacturing for advancing quality outcomes and operational excellence.
Ability to apply risk management principles to decision making and operational priorities.
Works in a cleanroom and office setting; frequently moves about inside the cleanroom to accomplish process tasks or oversee operations; occasionally moves lab equipment and materials weighing up to 50 pounds; compressed gases and LN2 are used in this process.
Travel to domestic and international partner sites may be required (up to 20%).

cond_0117.intro:

[Company name masked]'s Biopharmaceutical Sciences and Manufacturing Operations (BSMO) organization brings together biology, technologies, and manufacturing capabilities to advance cell and gene therapies (CGT) for patients. In this role, you will work alongside process development and other CMC stakeholders to support manufacturability, tech transfer, troubleshooting, and manufacturing equipment for cell therapy and combination products, from clinical to early commercial manufacturing for our Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) program. You will help build and manage a newly-formed manufacturing engineering team and represent the manufacturing organization on cross-functional teams throughout [Company name masked].
The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering for Drug Substance Drug Product (DSDP) CMC Manufacturing will work with the broader organization to oversee [Company name masked]'s first-of-its-kind cell therapy combination product, supporting the launch of GMP Manufacturing Phase III (Pivotal) and Commercial stage gates. The role reports to the Director of Manufacturing Operations, DSDP Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) program. This position is central to GMP manufacturing of current and new generations of cell and combination products and requires prior knowledge of [Location masked], EU and UK Medical Device regulations in addition to GMP cell manufacturing experience.
This position will coordinate with cross-functional stakeholders to support MFG in technical transfer activities within [Company name masked] internal Process Development, Quality, Validation, Supply Chain, MFG sites and/or external Contract Manufacturing Organizations in support of developing operationally fit manufacture of cell and cell/device combination products for Cell & Genetic Therapy. The role will help build and promote a culture of Quality to meet business, quality, and regulatory objectives.
cond_0117.responsibilities:
Work with the manufacturing engineering team for DSDP cells and combination products, coordinating design reviews and documentation with a focus on designing for manufacturability.
Collaborate with relevant teams to propose and implement Drug Product Device and manufacturing engineering controls by integrating [Company name masked] QMS, production controls, and risk assessments.
Coordinate CMC Cell manufacturing project plans to support clinical development, submission, and approval of drug-device combination products for the Type 1 Diabetes pipeline within the internal manufacturing team.
Serve as the main point of contact for cross-functional teams to ensure that all activities supporting combination product manufacturing deliverables are aligned and on track.
Serve as the MFG lead for tech transfer of new cell and combination DSDP processes and products, working alongside internal and external partners.
Support and develop a team of subject matter experts and engineers to help troubleshoot manufacturing issues.
Support successful clinical and commercial batch disposition across [Company name masked]'s internal and external manufacturing sites.
Identify and share risks with relevant stakeholders and assist with risk mitigation plans as needed.
Coordinate MFG assessment, approval, and implementation of investigations and change controls.
Represent the manufacturing group in combination device programs; participate in complex projects involving medical devices and work alongside key stakeholders for alignment in strategic and operational planning.
Foster collaboration, problem solving, and solution-set thinking with a broad range of internal and external stakeholders at all levels of the organization.
Regularly coordinate with functional areas beyond CMC, such as Regulatory, Quality, Supply Chain, Technical Operations, and Clinical.
Review and help approve critical process parameters for cell and combination products from a manufacturing feasibility and operational efficiency standpoint.
Work with the team to plan and set a vision for upcoming new facility requirements for cell and combo products at manufacturing sites.
Participate in Operational and Capital budgets.
Develop and deliver key performance indicators (KPIs) in collaboration with MFG leadership.
Assign tasks to internal team members and working teams within a defined governance model.
Coordinate with workstream leads to share recommendations, decisions, actions, and other pertinent information related to the development and manufacturing of cell and combination products.
Create, revise, and review controlled documents including Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Batch Records for manufacturing.
cond_0117.requirements:

BS, Master's Degree, or PhD in life science, Chemical/Mechanical Engineering, or equivalent.
5–8+ Years of biopharma manufacturing experience or equivalent medical device combination product experience.
A minimum of 3 years of people management experience.

Strong knowledge of federal requirements for GMP manufacturing (21 CFR 210, 211) and Quality Systems (21 CFR 820).
Comprehensive knowledge of Design Controls per 21 CFR 820.
Strong understanding of Manufacturing Engineering principles in GMP and relevant regulatory requirements for cell and combination products.
Strong experience managing cross-functional teams involved in the development, scale-up, technology transfer, and manufacturing of therapeutic combination products in a GMP environment.
Expertise in cell processing and culture technologies for clinical materials production.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to effectively communicate complex ideas and goals to various team members and stakeholders.
Preferred Requirements
Broad medical device/combination device technical knowledge of current industry trends.
Proven ability to develop strategies and lead improvement projects.
Experience with Root Cause Analysis and other Operational Excellence methodologies.
Strong understanding of medical device related combination therapies.
In-depth knowledge of the development process, including scale-up and manufacturing, for combination products.
Leads with emotional intelligence and is agile in complex and uncertain situations.
Strong leadership through a partnership and engagement approach with manufacturing for advancing quality outcomes and operational excellence.
Ability to apply risk management principles to decision making and operational priorities.
Excellent interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with cross-functional teams and external vendors.
Environment
Works in a cleanroom and office setting. Frequently moves about inside the cleanroom to accomplish process tasks or oversee operations. Occasionally moves lab equipment and materials weighing up to 50 pounds. Compressed gases and LN2 are used in this process.

[Company name masked]'s Biopharmaceutical Sciences and Manufacturing Operations (BSMO) organization brings together biology, technologies, and manufacturing capabilities to deliver cell and gene therapies (CGT) to patients. The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering will be responsible for designing for manufacturability, tech transfer, troubleshooting, and manufacturing equipment of cell therapy and combination products, from clinical to early commercial manufacturing for our Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) program. This leader will build and manage a newly-formed manufacturing engineering team. The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering will coordinate with process development and other CMC stakeholders to set strategic directions and ensure successful project outcomes. This leader will also represent the manufacturing organization on cross-functional teams throughout [Company name masked].
The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering for Drug Substance Drug Product (DSDP) CMC Manufacturing will be a strategic leader building and overseeing a new organization to oversee [Company name masked]'s first of its kind cell therapy combination product, covering GMP Manufacturing Phase III (Pivotal) and Commercial stage gates. The role reports to the Director of Manufacturing Operations, DSDP Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) program. The position is central to GMP manufacturing of current and new generations of cell and combination products and requires prior knowledge of [Location masked], EU and UK Medical Device regulations in addition to GMP cell manufacturing experience.
This position will work with cross-functional stakeholders to lead MFG in technical transfer activities within [Company name masked] internal Process Development, Quality, Validation, Supply Chain, MFG sites and/or external Contract Manufacturing Organizations in support of operationally fit manufacture of cell and cell/device combination products for Cell & Genetic Therapy. The role will be responsible for building and promoting a culture of Quality to meet business, quality, and regulatory objectives.
cond_0169.responsibilities:
Build and manage a manufacturing engineering team for DSDP cells and combination products.
Act as primary technical and engineering manufacturing lead for design reviews and documentation, with focus on designing for manufacturability.
Implement and drive Drug Product Device and manufacturing engineering controls by integrating [Company name masked] QMS, production controls, and risk assessments.
Drive CMC Cell manufacturing project plans to support clinical development, submission, and approval of drug-device combination product for the Type 1 Diabetes pipeline within the internal manufacturing team.
Serve as the main point of contact for cross-functional teams to ensure that all activities driving combination product manufacturing deliverables are aligned and on track.
Serve as the MFG lead for tech transfer of new cell and combination DSDP processes and products.
Develop and lead a team of subject matter experts and engineers to troubleshoot manufacturing issues.
Support successful clinical and commercial batch disposition across [Company name masked]'s internal and external manufacturing sites.
Identify and communicate risks and assist with risk mitigation plans as necessary.
Oversee MFG assessment, approval, and implementation of investigations and change controls.
Represent the manufacturing group in combination device programs; participate in complex projects involving medical devices and coordinate with key stakeholders on strategic and operational planning and delivery of business and financial priorities.
Interface with functional areas beyond CMC, such as Regulatory, Quality, Supply Chain, Technical Operations, and Clinical, as required by project needs.
Review and approve critical process parameters for cell and combination products from a manufacturing feasibility and operational efficiency standpoint.
Plan and set a vision for upcoming new facility requirements for cell and combination products at manufacturing sites.
Participate in operational and capital budgets.
Develop and deliver key performance indicators (KPIs) in coordination with MFG leadership.
Assign tasks to internal team members and working teams within a defined governance model.
Coordinate with workstream leads to relay recommendations, decisions, actions, and other pertinent information related to the development and manufacturing of the cell and combination product.
Create, revise, and review controlled documents including Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Batch Records for manufacturing.
cond_0169.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
BS, Master's Degree, or PhD in life science, Chemical/Mechanical Engineering, or equivalent.
5–8+ Years of biopharma manufacturing experience or equivalent medical device combination product experience.
Minimum of 3 years of people management experience.
Knowledge of GMP, FDA, and EMA regulatory requirements applicable to Device and/or Combination products.
Strong knowledge of federal requirements for GMP manufacturing (21 CFR 210, 211) and Quality Systems (21 CFR 820).
Comprehensive knowledge of Design Controls per 21 CFR 820.
Strong understanding of Manufacturing Engineering principles in GMP and relevant regulatory requirements for cell and combination products.
Strong understanding of medical device related combination therapies.
Experience with Root Cause Analysis and other Operational Excellence methods.
Expertise in cell processing and culture technologies for clinical materials production.
Preferred Requirements
Broad medical device/combination device technical knowledge of current industry trends.
Proven ability to develop strategies and lead improvement projects.
Strong experience managing cross-functional teams involved in development, scale-up, technology transfer, and manufacturing of therapeutic combination products in a GMP environment.
In-depth knowledge of the development process, including scale-up and manufacturing, for combination products.
Leads with emotional intelligence and is able to navigate complex and uncertain situations.
Ability to apply risk management principles to decision making and operational priorities.
Strong written communication and clear, direct verbal reporting, with the ability to convey complex ideas to team members and stakeholders.
Strong leadership through a partnership approach with manufacturing for advancing quality outcomes and operational excellence.
Works in a cleanroom and office setting. Frequently moves about inside the cleanroom to accomplish process tasks or oversee operations. Occasionally moves lab equipment and materials weighing up to 50 pounds. Compressed gases and LN2 are used in this process.
Travel to domestic and international partner sites may be required (up to 20%).

We make recruiting decisions based on your experience and skills. We value your passion to discover, invent, simplify and build.

cond_0219.intro:
We are looking for a Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering to join our team.
[Company name masked]'s Biopharmaceutical Sciences and Manufacturing Operations (BSMO) organization brings together biology, technologies, and manufacturing capabilities to deliver cell and gene therapies (CGT) to patients. The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering will be responsible for designing for manufacturability, tech transfer, troubleshooting and manufacturing equipment of cell therapy and combination products, from clinical to early commercial manufacturing for our growing Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) program. This leader will build and manage a newly-formed manufacturing engineering team. The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering will collaborate closely with process development and other CMC stakeholders to set strategic directions and ensure successful project outcomes. Additionally, this leader will represent the manufacturing organization on cross-functional teams throughout [Company name masked].
The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering for Drug Substance Drug Product (DSDP) CMC Manufacturing will be a strategic leader building and overseeing a new organization to oversee [Company name masked]'s first of its kind cell therapy combination product, foreseeing the launch of GMP Manufacturing Phase III (Pivotal) and Commercial stage gates. The role reports to the Director of Manufacturing Operations, DSDP Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) program. The position is key to GMP manufacturing of current and new generations of cell and combination products and should possess prior knowledge of the [Location masked], EU and UK Medical Device regulations in addition to GMP cell manufacturing experience.
This position will partner with cross-functional stakeholders to lead MFG in technical transfer activities within [Company name masked] internal Process Development, Quality, Validation, Supply chain, MFG sites and/or to external Contract Manufacturing Organization in support of developing operationally fit manufacture of cell and cell/device combination products for Cell & Genetic Therapy. The role will be responsible for inspiring/building/promoting a culture of Quality and to meet business, quality, and regulatory objectives.
cond_0219.responsibilities:
Build and manage a manufacturing engineering team for DSDP cells and combination products. Act as primary technical and engineering manufacturing lead design reviews, documentation with focus on designing for manufacturability. Implement, propose and drive the implementation of Drug Product Device and manufacturing engineering controls by integrating [Company name masked] QMS, production controls, risk assessments. Drive CMC Cell manufacturing project plans to support clinical development, submission, and approval of drug-device combination product to support the Type 1 Diabetes pipeline within internal manufacturing team. Serve as the main point of contact for cross-functional teams to ensure that all activities driving combination product manufacturing deliverables are aligned and on track. Serve as the MFG lead for tech transfer of new cell and combination DSDP processes and products. Develop, foster, and lead a team of highly driven subject matter experts and engineers to trouble shoot manufacturing issues. Support successful Clinical and commercial batch disposition across [Company name masked]'s internal and external manufacturing sites. Identify and communicate risks and assist with risk mitigation plans as necessary. Oversees MFG assessment, approval and implementation of investigations and change controls. Represent manufacturing group in combination device programs- participate in complex project involving medical device and partner with key stakeholders for alignment in strategic and operational planning and delivery of business & financial priorities and goals. Foster collaboration, problem solving, and solution-set thinking with the ability to interface with a broad range of internal and external stakeholders at all levels of the organization. Regularly interacts with functional areas beyond CMC, such as Regulatory, Quality, Supply Chain, Technical Operations and Clinical. Review and approve the critical process parameters for cell and combination products from manufacturing feasibility and operational efficiency standpoint. Strategically plan and set a vision to lay out upcoming new facility requirements for cell and combo products at manufacturing sites. Participate in Operational and Capital budgets. Develop and delivery on key performance indicators (KPIs) in collaboration with MFG leadership. Assign tasks to internal team members and working teams, within a defined governance model. Collaborate with workstream leads to relay recommendations, decisions, actions, and other pertinent information related to the development and manufacturing of the cell and combination product. Create, revise, and review controlled documents including Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Batch Records for manufacturing.
Knowledge And Skills
Strong understanding of Manufacturing Engineering principles in GMP and relevant regulatory requirements for cell and combination products. Comprehensive knowledge of Design Controls per 21 CFR 820. Strategic leader with excellent people management and staff development background. Highly driven and self-motivated with out of the box thinking mindset. Capable of delivering quality results within tight deadlines. Strong understanding of medical device related combination therapies. Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to effectively communicate complex ideas and goals to various team members and stakeholders. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to lead and work effectively with cross-functional teams and external vendors. In-depth knowledge of the development process, including scale-up and manufacturing, for combination products.
cond_0219.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
BS, Master's Degree or PhD in life science, Chemical/Mechanical engineering, or equivalent practical experience.
Around 5–8 years of biopharma manufacturing experience, or equivalent experience with medical device combination products, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Working knowledge of GMP, FDA and EMA regulatory requirements applicable to Device and/or Combination products.
Around 3 years of people management experience.
Familiarity with federal requirements for GMP manufacturing (21CFR 210, 211) and Quality Systems (21CFR 820).
Experience with cross-functional teams involved in development, scale-up, technology transfer and manufacturing of therapeutic combination products in a GMP environment.
Ability to communicate effectively and a track record working in a matrix environment; willingness to build and promote a culture of Quality.
Preferred Requirements
Broad medical device/combination device technical knowledge of current industry trends.
Experience with Root Cause Analysis and other Operational Excellence approaches.
Background in cell processing and culture technologies for clinical materials production.
Ability to apply risk management principles to decision making and operational priorities.
Experience developing strategies and leading improvement projects.
Openness to leading with emotional intelligence and being adaptable in complex and uncertain situations.
Background in advancing quality outcomes through partnership and engagement with manufacturing teams.
Environment
Works in a cleanroom and office setting. Frequently move about inside the cleanroom to accomplish process tasks or oversee operations. Occasionally moves lab equipment and materials weighing up to 50 pounds. Compressed gasses and LN2 are used in this process.
Other Requirements
Travel to domestic and international partner sites may be required (up to 20%).

[Company name masked]'s Biopharmaceutical Sciences and Manufacturing Operations (BSMO) organization brings together the best biology, technologies, and enhanced manufacturing capabilities to bring cutting-edge, transformative cell and gene therapies (CGT) to patients as quickly as possible. The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering will be responsible for designing for manufacturability, tech transfer, troubleshooting and manufacturing equipment of cell therapy and combination products, from clinical to early commercial manufacturing for our growing Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) program. This leader will build and manage a newly-formed manufacturing engineering team. The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering will collaborate closely with process development and other CMC stakeholders to set strategic directions and ensure successful project outcomes. Additionally, this leader will represent the manufacturing organization on cross-functional teams throughout [Company name masked].
The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering for Drug Substance Drug Product (DSDP) CMC Manufacturing will be a strategic leader building and overseeing a new organization to oversee [Company name masked]'s first of its kind cell therapy combination product, foreseeing the launch of GMP Manufacturing Phase III (Pivotal) and Commercial stage gates. The role reports to the Director of Manufacturing Operations, DSDP Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) program. The position is key to GMP manufacturing of current and new generations of cell and combination products and should possess prior knowledge of the [Location masked], EU and UK Medical Device regulations in addition to GMP cell manufacturing experience.
This position will partner with cross-functional stakeholders to lead MFG in technical transfer activities within [Company name masked] internal Process Development, Quality, Validation, Supply chain, MFG sites and/or to external Contract Manufacturing Organization in support of developing operationally fit manufacture of cell and cell/device combination products for Cell & Genetic Therapy. The role will be responsible for inspiring/building/promoting a culture of Quality and to meet business, quality, and regulatory objectives. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the engineering and regulatory logic behind cell and combination product manufacturing.
cond_0229.responsibilities: Build and manage a manufacturing engineering team for DSDP cells and combination products. Act as primary technical and engineering manufacturing lead design reviews, documentation with focus on designing for manufacturability. Implement, propose and drive the implementation of Drug Product Device and manufacturing engineering controls by integrating [Company name masked] QMS, production controls, risk assessments. Drive CMC Cell manufacturing project plans to support clinical development, submission, and approval of drug-device combination product to support the Type 1 Diabetes pipeline within internal manufacturing team. Serve as the main point of contact for cross-functional teams to ensure that all activities driving combination product manufacturing deliverables are aligned and on track. Serve as the MFG lead for tech transfer of new cell and combination DSDP processes and products. Develop, foster, and lead a team of highly driven subject matter experts and engineers to trouble shoot manufacturing issues. Support successful Clinical and commercial batch disposition across [Company name masked]'s internal and external manufacturing sites. Identify and communicate risks and assist with risk mitigation plans as necessary. Oversees MFG assessment, approval and implementation of investigations and change controls. Represent manufacturing group in combination device programs- participate in complex project involving medical device and partner with key stakeholders for alignment in strategic and operational planning and delivery of business & financial priorities and goals. Foster collaboration, problem solving, and solution-set thinking with the ability to interface with a broad range of internal and external stakeholders at all levels of the organization. Regularly interacts with functional areas beyond CMC, such as Regulatory, Quality, Supply Chain, Technical Operations and Clinical. Review and approve the critical process parameters for cell and combination products from manufacturing feasibility and operational efficiency standpoint. Strategically plan and set a vision to lay out upcoming new facility requirements for cell and combo products at manufacturing sites. Participate in Operational and Capital budgets. Develop and delivery on key performance indicators (KPIs) in collaboration with MFG leadership. Assign tasks to internal team members and working teams, within a defined governance model. Collaborate with workstream leads to relay recommendations, decisions, actions, and other pertinent information related to the development and manufacturing of the cell and combination product. Create, revise, and review controlled documents including Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Batch Records for manufacturing.
cond_0229.requirements:
Strong understanding of Manufacturing Engineering principles in GMP and relevant regulatory requirements for cell and combination products. Comprehensive knowledge of Design Controls per 21 CFR 820. Strategic leader with excellent people management and staff development background. Highly driven and self-motivated with out of the box thinking mindset. Capable of delivering quality results within tight deadlines. Strong understanding of medical device related combination therapies. Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to effectively communicate complex ideas and goals to various team members and stakeholders. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to lead and work effectively with cross-functional teams and external vendors. In-depth knowledge of the development process, including scale-up and manufacturing, for combination products.
BS, Master's Degree or PhD in life science, Chemical/ Mechanical engineering or equivalent. 5-8 Plus years of biopharma manufacturing experience or the equivalent medical device combination product experience. Knowledge of GMP, FDA and EMA regulatory requirements applicable to Device and/or Combination products. Broad medical device /combination device technical knowledge of current industry trends. Proven ability to develop strategies and lead improvement projects. Experience with Root Cause Analysis, and other Operational Excellence experience. A minimum of 3 years people management experience. Strong Knowledge of federal requirements for GMP manufacturing (21CFR 210,211) and Quality Systems (21CFR 820). Excellent communication skills and a track record working in a matrix environment; Influencing/building/promoting a culture of Quality. Leads with emotional intelligence and strives to be agile in complex and uncertain situations. Strong leadership through a partnership and engagement approach with manufacturing for advancing quality outcomes and operational excellence. Ability to apply risk management principles to decision making and operational priorities. Strong experience in managing cross-functional teams involved in the development, scale-up, technology transfer and manufacturing of therapeutic combination products in a GMP environment. Expertise in cell processing and culture technologies for clinical materials production.
Works in a cleanroom and office setting. Frequently move about inside the cleanroom to accomplish process tasks or oversee operations. Occasionally moves lab equipment and materials weighing up to 50 pounds. Compressed gasses and LN2 are used in this process.
Travel to domestic and international partner sites may be required (up to 20%).

cond_0231.intro:
[Company name masked]'s Biopharmaceutical Sciences and Manufacturing Operations (BSMO) organization brings together biology, technologies, and manufacturing capabilities to deliver cell and gene therapies (CGT) to patients. The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering will be responsible for designing for manufacturability, tech transfer, troubleshooting and manufacturing equipment of cell therapy and combination products, from clinical to early commercial manufacturing for our growing Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) program. This leader will build and manage a newly-formed manufacturing engineering team and will regularly connect with process development and other CMC stakeholders to set strategic directions and ensure successful project outcomes. Additionally, this leader will represent the manufacturing organization on cross-functional teams throughout [Company name masked].
The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering for Drug Substance Drug Product (DSDP) CMC Manufacturing will be a strategic leader building and overseeing a new organization to oversee [Company name masked]'s first of its kind cell therapy combination product, foreseeing the launch of GMP Manufacturing Phase III (Pivotal) and Commercial stage gates. The role reports to the Director of Manufacturing Operations, DSDP Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) program. The position is central to GMP manufacturing of current and new generations of cell and combination products and should possess prior knowledge of the [Location masked], EU and UK Medical Device regulations in addition to GMP cell manufacturing experience.
This position will actively partner with cross-functional stakeholders to lead MFG in technical transfer activities within [Company name masked] internal Process Development, Quality, Validation, Supply chain, MFG sites and/or to external Contract Manufacturing Organizations in support of developing operationally fit manufacture of cell and cell/device combination products for Cell & Genetic Therapy. The role will be responsible for building and promoting a culture of Quality and to meet business, quality, and regulatory objectives.
cond_0231.responsibilities:
Build and manage a manufacturing engineering team for DSDP cells and combination products.
Act as primary technical and engineering manufacturing lead for design reviews and documentation, with a focus on designing for manufacturability.
Implement, propose and drive the implementation of Drug Product Device and manufacturing engineering controls by integrating [Company name masked] QMS, production controls, and risk assessments.
Drive CMC Cell manufacturing project plans to support clinical development, submission, and approval of drug-device combination product to support the Type 1 Diabetes pipeline within the internal manufacturing team.
Serve as the main point of contact for cross-functional teams, regularly communicating with all relevant groups to ensure that activities driving combination product manufacturing deliverables are aligned and on track.
Serve as the MFG lead for tech transfer of new cell and combination DSDP processes and products.
Develop, foster, and lead a team of subject matter experts and engineers to troubleshoot manufacturing issues.
Support successful clinical and commercial batch disposition across [Company name masked]'s internal and external manufacturing sites.
Identify and communicate risks and assist with risk mitigation plans as necessary.
Oversee MFG assessment, approval and implementation of investigations and change controls.
Represent the manufacturing group in combination device programs — actively participate in complex projects involving medical devices and stay in close contact with key stakeholders for alignment in strategic and operational planning and delivery of business and financial priorities and goals.
Foster collaboration, problem solving, and solution-set thinking, with the ability to interface regularly with a broad range of internal and external stakeholders at all levels of the organization.
Regularly interact with functional areas beyond CMC, such as Regulatory, Quality, Supply Chain, Technical Operations and Clinical.
Review and approve critical process parameters for cell and combination products from a manufacturing feasibility and operational efficiency standpoint.
Strategically plan and set a vision for upcoming new facility requirements for cell and combo products at manufacturing sites.
Participate in operational and capital budgets.
Develop and deliver key performance indicators (KPIs) in collaboration with MFG leadership.
Assign tasks to internal team members and working teams within a defined governance model.
Collaborate with workstream leads to relay recommendations, decisions, actions, and other pertinent information related to the development and manufacturing of the cell and combination product.
Create, revise, and review controlled documents including Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Batch Records for manufacturing.
cond_0231.requirements:
BS, Master's Degree or PhD in life science, Chemical/Mechanical engineering or equivalent.
5–8+ Years of biopharma manufacturing experience or equivalent medical device combination product experience.
Strong understanding of Manufacturing Engineering principles in GMP and relevant regulatory requirements for cell and combination products.
Comprehensive knowledge of Design Controls per 21 CFR 820.
Strong Knowledge of federal requirements for GMP manufacturing (21 CFR 210, 211) and Quality Systems (21 CFR 820).
Knowledge of GMP, FDA and EMA regulatory requirements applicable to Device and/or Combination products.
Broad medical device/combination device technical knowledge of current industry trends.
In-depth knowledge of the development process, including scale-up and manufacturing, for combination products.
Strong understanding of medical device related combination therapies.
Expertise in cell processing and culture technologies for clinical materials production.
Strong experience managing cross-functional teams involved in the development, scale-up, technology transfer and manufacturing of therapeutic combination products in a GMP environment.
Proven ability to develop strategies and lead improvement projects.
Experience with Root Cause Analysis and other Operational Excellence methodologies.
A minimum of 3 years people management experience.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to clearly explain complex ideas and goals to various team members and stakeholders.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to lead and work effectively with cross-functional teams and external vendors.
Track record working in a matrix environment; influencing and promoting a culture of Quality.
Leads with emotional intelligence and is able to stay effective in complex and uncertain situations.
Strong leadership through a partnership and engagement approach with manufacturing for advancing quality outcomes and operational excellence.
Ability to apply risk management principles to decision making and operational priorities.
Works in a cleanroom and office setting; frequently moves about inside the cleanroom to accomplish process tasks or oversee operations.
Occasionally moves lab equipment and materials weighing up to 50 pounds.
Comfortable working with compressed gases and LN2 used in this process.

cond_0232.intro:
